# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-39 (Extended v243)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to autumn Year 10, and 1784-1820 (Marseilles/Pharaon timeline). Key Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Charlemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Champs-Élysées, Rue Saint-Honoré, Luxembourg Garden, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Temple, sewers (Sainte-Avoye, Louvre, Montmartre, belt, Amelot, Beautreillis), Marais, Blancs-Manteaux, Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, Rue de l'Écharpe, Rue Pavée, Rue des Trois-Pavillons, Saint-Paul church, Rue Beautreillis near Arsenal, Grand Sewer, Rue de l'Hôpital, Père-Lachaise cemetery, Rue Mondétour, Tuileries, Rue Saint-Jacques, Rue de la Jussienne, Rue Coq-Héron, Rue Bussy, Lyons, Grenoble. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Wilholt, Torton, Yarlby, Gagny, Lagny, Gulhaven. Marseilles: La Canebière, Rue de Noailles, Allées de Meilhan, Rue du Grand Cours, Rue de l'Homme Armé, Medusa fountain, Palais de Justice, Accoules clock-tower, Rue Caisserie, Rue Saint-Laurent, Rue Taramis, La Consigne, Frioul, Pilon, Porto-Ferrajo, Naples, Elba, Island of Elba, Point des Catalans, Ile Ratonneau, Rue de la Loge, Catalans, Madrid, Cape Pharo, Cape de Morgiou, Château d'If. **Timeline: 1814-1820 Marseilles; 1 March 1814 Dantès' arrest; spring/summer Year 10 English subplot; autumn Year 10 current time in Chapter 39.**

## English Subplot Summary (through Chapter 39, autumn Year 10)

**Established solemn promises**: Semor swore to Isric Thornmere to rebuild fallen wall at Kelmere (summer Year 9). Elra gave Matho promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven; Pelia gave Fenelle promise to plant orchard above Salcombe (summer Year 7); Movie swore to Nerine promise to plant orchard above Wilholt (autumn Year 7); Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair chapel roof at Kelmere (winter Year 8); Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest; Kassa's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Yera Haskick gave Lurald Stenworth solemn promise to carry sealed letter to Quenford (winter Year 9). Eldest daughter of Lura Haskick kept promise made to Nerine Prydenridge: chapel roof repair at Kelmere completed by harvest (winter Year 9). Fewyn gave Havus Stenworth solemn promise to carry sealed letter to Salcombe (winter Year 9). Luena gave husband of Yera Stenworth solemn promise to pay old debt owed to Haskick family (winter Year 9). Sebin swore to youngest daughter of Havus Stenworth to repair roof of chapel at Wilholt (spring Year 10). Harine swore to wife of Sebin Brackick to teach children of Kelmere their letters (summer Year 10).

**Chapter 34-35 migrations**: Taric Corrley moved from Dungate to Kelmere with Kassa Stenson. Luena Stenenridge's only son moved from Ostcombe to Elmhaven. Pelde Stenworth married Sebin Brackick at Torton; couple lived in Torton thereafter. Fewyn Stenworth moved from Gulhaven to Yarlby with Havus. Pelia Lindmere moved to Yarlby with Rorald Lindmere. Havie Prydenridge found work in Staveford, moved there; Isric Thornmere followed her within the month. Youngest daughter of Fewyn Stenworth was apprenticed anew and became a herbalist. Youngest son of Nelan Brackick was apprenticed anew and became a weaver.

**Summer Year 10 births and changes**: Ismira Stenson died from festering wound; buried at Kelmere; bone compass went to Matho Stenson. Son born to Luvie Prydenridge and Semor Brackick, named Brevus Brackick; family lived in Ostcombe. Daughter born to Pelde Stenworth and Sebin Brackick, named Elvie Brackick; family lived in Torton. Son born to Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge, named Madan Prydenridge; family lived in Kelmere. Febin Prydenridge packed single trunk and moved from Kelmere to Elmhaven. Davus was apprenticed anew and became a mason. Daughter born to Movie Prydenridge and Thizek Stenenridge, named Kamira Stenenridge; family lived in Elmhaven.

**Chapter 38-39 summer/autumn scenes and movements**: Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; wind carried salt and tar smell; carts loaded with turnips creaked past well; smoke lay flat over fields; frost silvered hedges overnight; rain threatened but held off; gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps; baker's boy was late, line at oven grew long; crooked sun chalked on forge wall. Multiple characters counted coins twice and came up penny short; complained of aching back; read almanac aloud mispronouncing saints; laughed at stories nobody else found funny; mended torn sleeves by window; fell asleep in chairs before fire caught; walked long way round to avoid muddy square. **Ilrald Prydenridge left Torton and settled in Wilwick. Dalis left Torton and settled in Yarlby. Harine went along to live in Wilwick as well.** RUMOR—Isric Thornmere told Havie Prydenridge old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar. RUMOR—In letter Semor Brackick burned, youngest son of Malis Prydenridge revealed old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar. **Late one night Kassa Brackick confided to Davus that Stenenridge mill ledger was rewritten after flood.**

## Marseilles/Pharaon Subplot (1814-1820): Dantès' Imprisonment and Escape

**Edmond Dantès' arrest and Villefort's conspiracy (1 March 1814)**: Young sailor jumped into skiff at La Canebière. Reported Captain Leclere dead; would become captain with M. Morrel's aid. Wedding feast at La Réserve with Mercédès; betrothal announced. Danglars and Fernand conspired; Danglars wrote denunciation with left hand naming Dantès as Murat's agent. Magistrate arrested Dantès during feast. Villefort interrogated Dantès about commission to deliver letter in Paris to Noirtier (Villefort's father). **Villefort destroyed fatal letter—only proof against Dantès.** Mercédès came to Villefort's door inquiring; Villefort closed door. **Dantès was doomed.** Villefort reported conspiracy to King Louis XVIII, received Legion of Honor cross. **Noirtier—Villefort's father—disguised himself: cut whiskers, changed cravat, wore dark brown coat, narrow-brimmed hat, walked past sentries with bamboo switch.**

**Dantès' psychological dissolution (1 March 1814–Year 4+)**: Boarded boat to Frioul; saw Point des Catalans where Mercédès dwelt; reached Château d'If. Locked in bare underground chamber. Marked plaster fragment daily with 30 July 1816 reckoning. Expected release in fortnight; waited nearly four years. Governor transferred; Edmond became number 34. At end of second year ceased marking time. Sustained by pride, then doubt, then supplication. Asked for companion; refused. Gloom, rage, blasphemies ensued. Contemplation of abyss offered strange consolation. **Resolved: "I wish to die." Chose starvation; swore oath.** Cast out food twice daily until had not strength to rise. **Heard mysterious scratching—subterranean workman mining way. Raised eyes to heaven, felt gratitude. "If neighbor would not come, he would go to neighbor."** Worked tirelessly extracting plaster and stone. **Noted prisoner on other side ceased labor. After hours, iron met smooth surface—beam blocking hole. Must dig above or under it.**

**Abbé Faria revealed (Chapter 38)**: **Dantès made passionate plea: "Oh, I am a Christian," cried he. "I swear to you by him who died for us that naught shall induce me to breathe one syllable to my jailers; but I conjure you do not abandon me... If you are young, I will be your comrade; if you are old, I will be your son... I shall love you as I loved my father."** **Following night Dantès rose, dispersed fragments, pushed bed back, gave himself to happiness. At slightest noise bounded towards door; if jailer examined opening, he would kill him with water jug.** **Next morning appeared head, then shoulders, then body: small stature man, hair blanched by suffering rather than age. Deep-set penetrating eye beneath thick gray eyebrow, long black beard to breast. Thin deeply furrowed face; bold outline showed mental rather than physical exercise. Numbered sixty or sixty-five years; vigor showed aged more from captivity than time. Received enthusiastic greeting with pleasure.** **Stranger: "I am Abbé Faria, imprisoned since 1811; previously confined three years in Fenestrelle fortress. In 1811 transferred to Piedmont. Learned Napoleon had son named king of Rome. Did not expect colossus overthrown. Then who reigns—Napoleon II?"** **Faria imprisoned because in 1807 he dreamed plan Napoleon realized in 1811; like Machiavelli, desired to alter Italy's political face, sought one large compact powerful empire instead of petty principalities. Fancied he found his Caesar Borgia in crowned simpleton who betrayed him. Plan of Alexander VI and Clement VII will never succeed; Italy fated to misfortune. Acknowledged: "I am poor mad prisoner of Château d'If, permitted many years to amuse visitors with my insanity."**

**Faria's scholarly achievements**: **Possessed five thousand volumes in Rome library; found one hundred fifty well-chosen books possess all man need. Devoted three years studying them, knew nearly by heart. Since imprisonment, slight memory effort enables recalling contents. Recites Thucydides, Xenophon, Plutarch, Titus Livius, Tacitus, Strada, Jornandes, Dante, Montaigne, Shakespeare, Spinoza, Machiavelli, Bossuet.** **Made vocabulary of necessary words; knows one thousand, though dictionaries contain one hundred thousand. Not fluent but explains wants readily.** **Made excellent pens from whiting-head cartilages (maigre days). Wrote _A Treatise on Possibility of General Monarchy in Italy_—entire work, fruits of whole life's thoughts, meditated in Colosseum's shades, at St. Mark's column, Arno's borders. Will make one large quarto. Wrote _finis_ at end of sixty-eighth strip week ago. Tore up two shirts and handkerchiefs to complete pages. Wrote with own blood for important notes.** **For ink, dissolved soot from former closed fireplace in Sunday wine. Better ink cannot be desired.** **Used ray of light and wall lines tracing double motion of earth and ellipse round sun to ascertain precise hour more accurately than watch.** **Made slender six-inch stick resembling painting-brush handle, with whiting cartilage tied by thread to end, pointed and divided nib like ordinary pen.**

**Faria's escape plan and Dantès' revelation (Chapter 38)**: **Proposed new escape: "We must pierce corridor by forming side opening about middle like cross top. You will lay plans accurately; shall get into gallery; kill sentinel who guards it, make escape."** **Explained why did not kill sentinel: "Natural repugnance to crime prevented thinking of it... man loathes idea of blood."** **On celebrated escapes: "Since imprisonment, thought over most celebrated cases. Rarely successful. Those crowned with full success long meditated and carefully arranged: Duc de Beaufort from Vincennes, Abbé Dubuquoi from Fort l'Evêque, Latude from Bastille. Then those for which chance affords opportunity—those are best. Let us wait patiently for favorable moment, profit by it."** **Once thought removing iron bars from window and letting himself down; would merely drop into inner court; renounced as too risky. Carefully preserved rope ladder of cords twenty-five to thirty feet, concealed behind fitting stone at bed's head—unforeseen opportunities chance brings.**

**Dantès' history and accusation discovery (Chapter 38)**: **Dantès recounted voyage to India, Levant voyages, last cruise with Captain Leclere's death, packet receipt, grand marshal interview, letter to Noirtier, Marseilles arrival, father interview, affection for Mercédès, nuptial feast, arrest, examination, Palais de Justice detention, Château d'If imprisonment. From this point: blank. Did not know length of imprisonment.** **Faria meditated: "Unless wicked ideas take root in depraved mind, human nature revolts at crime. From artificial civilization originate wants, vices, false tastes stifling good feelings, leading to guilt. Axiom: discover bad action author—seek person to whom perpetration advantageous. To whom could your disappearance serve?"** **Dantès revealed: one sailor Fernand had ill-will, quarrel, refused duel challenge. Denunciation read: "King's attorney informed by throne and religion friend that Edmond Dantès, mate on _Pharaon_, arrived from Smyrna, touched Naples and Porto-Ferrajo, intrusted by Murat with packet for usurper; by usurper, letter for Bonapartist Club Paris. Guilt proof procured by immediate arrest—letter will be found about person, father's residence, or cabin on _Pharaon_."** **Dantès identified third person: tailor Caderousse, very drunk. On table: pens, ink, paper. "Oh, heartless, treacherous scoundrels!" Pressed hand to throbbing brows.** **Dantès asked: "How did I undergo no second examination, never brought to trial, above all condemned without sentence passed?"** **Faria responded: "Altogether different, more serious matter. Ways of justice frequently too dark to penetrate. All hitherto done child's play. If wish harder business, must assist by most minute information on every point."** **At these words—thunderbolt, hell's yawning gulf—Dantès transfixed with horror. Starting up, clasped hands round head as though to prevent brain bursting, exclaimed, "His father! His father!"** **Bright light shot through Dantès' mind: Villefort's change during examination, letter destruction, exacted promise, supplicating magistrate's tones—all returned with stunning force. Staggered against wall, hurried to opening, said, "I must be alone, to think over all this."**

**Dantès' resolution (Chapter 38-39)**: **In dungeon threw himself on bed, where turnkey found him evening visit with fixed gaze, contracted features, dumb and motionless as statue. During profound meditation hours (seemed only minutes), formed fearful resolution, bound himself to fulfillment by solemn oath.**

**Chapter 39 opening**: **Autumn of tenth year arrived. Dantès roused from reverie by Faria's voice inviting him to share supper. Abbé's reputation of being harmlessly, amusingly mad procured unusual privileges: finer bread than usual prison fare, small wine quantity each Sunday. This was Sunday; abbé came to ask young companion share luxuries.**

## Marius and Cosette: Courtship to Death Vigil

**Spring Year 6 confessions through barricade**: Marius revealed orphan status, lawyer profession, father colonel-hero. Cosette revealed convent upbringing, dead mother, father M. Fauchelevent. Éponine died leading Marius to barricade. Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed. Shot broke collar bone.

**Medical recovery and wedding (1 February 1833)**: Doctor declared recovery assured. Learned Cosette was not daughter of old man she called father; another Fauchelevent was real father. Dowry: five hundred eighty thousand francs, constituted legacy by dead person desiring to remain unknown. **Wedding at church of Saint-Paul: Cosette wore white taffeta petticoat, Binche guipure robe, English point veil, pearl necklace, orange flower wreath. Route: Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. Jean Valjean rose, left unperceived during celebration.**

**Javert's death and estrangement**: Javert drowned in Seine. **RUMOR—Marius suspects Jean Valjean killed Javert in barricade.**

**Jean Valjean's revelation and withdrawal**: **Proclaimed: "I am an ex-convict."** Marius shocked, concluded Jean Valjean horrible workman but admirable work. Address changed to _you_, "Madame," "Monsieur Jean." Cosette became more gay, less tender. Complete extinction ensued. Neatly clad in black, emerged daily at same hour towards nightfall from Rue de l'Homme Armé. **He was eighty years old; before Marius' marriage, would have hardly been taken for fifty; that year counted for thirty.** Later confined to apartment, then bed. **Revealed black jet from England, white jet from Norway; invented substitution method; six hundred thousand francs made. Managed very well with glass goods. Adjured Marius: "Have no fear, six hundred thousand francs really belong to Cosette!"** **[Heard by God alone]: "All is over. I shall never see her more... What is frightful is to die without seeing her."** **Lies in Père-Lachaise cemetery vicinity common grave, far from elegant quarter, deserted corner beside old wall, beneath great yew tree over which climbs wild convolvulus.**

## Thénardier's Blackmail and Marius's Confrontation

**Thénardier's discovery and blackmail**: Through daughter Azelma tracking married pair, discovered Cosette was Madame la Baronne Pontmercy. **Offered to drive individual from family who has no right; claimed twenty thousand francs as price. Wore black cloth coat, silk waistcoat, boots, green glasses, plastered gray hair. With monkey agility, tore off spectacles, withdrew two quills from nose, took off face as man takes off hat.**

**Marius's confrontation and evidence**: Revealed Javert's suicide facts announced in _Moniteur_ 15 June 1832: Javert owed life to insurgent who fired into air instead of blowing out brains. **Marius possessed evidence, certain date, irrefragable proof. Condemned Thénardier as "infamous wretch," "liar," "calumniator," "villain." Noted witnessed Thénardier Jondrette in lair on Rue de l'Hôpital; succeeded only in glorifying Jean Valjean.** Offered twenty thousand francs total, ordered Thénardier to America with daughter; wife dead. **Thénardier set up as slave-dealer in America, morally irremediable.**
